changes.before: Use this when you need a precise measure for review. You can leave unknowns explicit; this does not authorize collecting data.
changes.after: Use this section to draft a specific measure that could later be reviewed or validated. Record any uncertainties or incomplete details as needed. Completing this field does not give permission to collect new data, but clarifies the measurement concept for discussion or planning.
changes.reason: Added context about the purpose and limits of this section to clarify when and why to use it, without implying any authority to collect data. Replaced "You can leave unknowns explicit" with direct instructions to note uncertainties and incomplete details. Explained the practical value of drafting a proposed measure for review or planning.

findings.finding: The revised field ('after') expands substantially beyond the source, changing the scope and meaning of the original instruction. The source simply states: "Use this when you need a precise measure for review. You can leave unknowns explicit; this does not authorize collecting data." The replacement introduces new claims ('could later be reviewed or validated', 'clarifies the measurement concept for discussion or planning') that are not supported by the source text. It also expands instructions by directing users to record uncertainties or incomplete details, which, while reasonable, are not present in the original source. The revision changes the intent from a narrow guidance on permissible drafting and explicitness to a broader process framing and adds practical implications not in the source. Per standard, source meaning and scope must be preserved.
